# Loader (Spinner)

Figma: [05f. Loader (Spinner)](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-927) · Family: 05 Feedback · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-09

Indeterminate loading indicators shown when the system is doing work but cannot communicate progress (no known duration, no percentage). 8 spinner styles to choose from: Ring (the canonical Syntropy primary), DotOrbit, WaveBars, BouncingDots, PulseRings, SquareMorph, Hourglass, and a custom SafqahBrand spinner using stacked coin discs. Each ships at 5 sizes (XS 16 → XL 64). Spinners do not animate in Figma - they show their at-rest visual identity. The doc page includes multi-frame keyframe sequences showing the motion intent, plus working CSS and Flutter animation code. NEW in Syntropy v2.0.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/loader/reference.png`

### SpinnerRing

Indeterminate loader: the canonical Syntropy spinner: a 270 degree brand-green arc that rotates. Use it for about 95% of indeterminate waits; pick one spinner style per surface and keep it consistent.

Level: atom

Use when:
- Inline status like fetching deals next to a label (Size=S)
- Centered in a Modal or BottomSheet while an investment processes (Size=L)
- Small indicator in a dense row (Size=XS)

Don't use when:
- Loading a list, card or grid with known shape: use SkeletonLine and SkeletonBlock
- Measurable progress or waits over 10 seconds: use ProgressBar
- A button that is submitting: use Button loading state

Accessibility: role=status with a text label ("Loading"); show only after 200ms; static under prefers-reduced-motion.

| Phase | `phase` | variant | 0, 1, 2, 3 | 0 |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Loaders are indeterminate progress indicators - they show that work is happening but cannot communicate progress, percentage, or estimated time. Unlike Skeleton (05e) which preserves the shape of incoming content, loaders are a single small visual that says "something is happening, please wait." They are used in contexts where the load has a known short duration but the shape of the result is irrelevant or unpredictable.

### When to use a Loader

- A button is processing an action - the spinner sits inside the button (use Button with State=loading).
- A modal or sheet is performing work and a centered spinner is sufficient.
- A page-level navigation transition where shape-matching is unnecessary.
- Background work indicators in a status bar or toast (use a small XS or S spinner).
- When the work has indeterminate length but is expected to be brief (1-5 seconds).

### When NOT to use a Loader

- Loading a list, grid, or card layout where shape matters - use Skeleton (05e). Spinners feel like a worse UX because the user does not see content shape immediately.
- Determinate progress - use ProgressBar (04j) which shows the actual percentage complete.
- Long operations (> 10 seconds) - show concrete progress (steps, percentage, ETA) instead.
- Sub-200ms work - show nothing. Spinners that flash briefly cause more anxiety than no indicator at all.

### Choosing which spinner

For 95% of cases, use the Ring spinner - it is the canonical Syntropy primary. The other 7 are for special contexts: SafqahBrand for branded loading screens, SquareMorph or Hourglass for distinctive non-circular contexts, DotOrbit or BouncingDots for chat / messaging / typing indicators, WaveBars for audio / media contexts, PulseRings for radar / scanning / detection contexts. Pick one spinner per product surface and use it consistently - mixing spinner styles within the same product feels chaotic.

### Anatomy - 8 spinners

Each spinner is its own component set with 5 size variants (XS 16, S 24, M 32, L 48, XL 64). They share the same Size axis but are otherwise distinct components - designers pick which spinner suits the context, then pick the size.

### Ring

The canonical Syntropy spinner. A 270° brand-green arc with rounded caps that rotates clockwise around its center. Stroke width scales with size (1.5px at XS, 4.5px at XL). Use this 95% of the time. CSS: `transform: rotate(...)` with 0.8s linear infinite duration.

### DotOrbit

Three brand-green dots arranged at 120° around a center, rotating as a group. The trailing dots fade with reduced opacity (1.0, 0.7, 0.4) to give a sense of motion direction. Use for chat / messaging contexts where the "typing" feel is appropriate. CSS: rotate the parent every 1s.

### WaveBars

Five vertical brand-green pill-shaped bars at staggered heights, creating a wave / audio-equalizer shape. In code each bar scaleY animates with a phase offset, giving the "rolling wave" effect. Use for audio playback, voice recording, or media-related contexts. CSS: per-bar scaleY animation with 80ms phase stagger.

### BouncingDots

Three brand-green dots in a horizontal row, each bouncing vertically with phase offsets. Reads as a "typing indicator" - used in chat, comments, AI-response-pending contexts. CSS: per-dot translateY animation with 200ms phase stagger.

### PulseRings

Three concentric brand-green stroked rings expanding outward and fading. Reads as "scanning" / "broadcasting" / "detecting". Use for location-finding, network-discovery, or status-polling contexts. CSS: per-ring scale + opacity animation with 333ms phase stagger.

### SquareMorph

A brand-green rounded square rotating around its center. Distinctive non-circular alternative to Ring. Use when the surrounding UI is heavy on circles and you want visual contrast. CSS: continuous rotation, 1s linear infinite.

### Hourglass

Two brand-green triangles meeting at the center forming an hourglass shape, rotating around its center. Strongly communicates "time is passing" - use for deliberate, slower waits (file uploads, processing operations). CSS: rotation with 1.5s ease-in-out timing for a heavier feel.

### SafqahBrand

Three stacked elliptical coin discs in brand-green, with the top coin animating up and down. Custom branded spinner tying to the Safqah investment / coin-stack theme. Use for branded loading screens (app boot, onboarding transitions, deal-purchase confirmations) where the product personality should come through. The bottom and middle discs have reduced opacity (0.4, 0.7) for depth.

### Sizes

5 sizes per spinner type (XS 16, S 24, M 32, L 48, XL 64). Pick the size based on the surface and the prominence the spinner needs. Stroke widths on Ring scale with size to keep visual weight consistent.

XS - 16px

Inside Button (use Button with State=loading instead), inline with body text, in a dense table cell. Almost always Ring style.

S - 24px

Inline next to a label ("Saving..." with a spinner), small status indicators, dense card UI.

M - 32px

Centered inside a small modal, a sheet, or a small empty container.

L - 48px

Centered inside a card, a section, or a modal where the spinner is the dominant element.

XL - 64px

Page-level full-screen loading, splash screens, branded loading transitions (use SafqahBrand here).

### In context - common patterns

5 canonical Safqah loader patterns. Pick the spinner style based on the context, then choose the size based on the surface.

### Pattern 1 - Button loading (XS Ring)

Inside a Button with State=loading. The button shows the spinner where its left icon would be, and the label changes to a verb-ing form ("Saving...", "Submitting..."). Do NOT build this with a separate spinner - use the Button component's built-in State=loading instead. Spinner: Ring XS. Most common loader pattern in Safqah.

### Pattern 2 - Inline with label (S Ring + text)

A small spinner next to inline text. Used in status rows ("Fetching deals..." with a spinner), bank-account verification, OTP send screens. Spinner: Ring S. Text-and-spinner combined as a horizontal flex row with 8px gap.

### Pattern 3 - Centered in modal (L Ring)

A medium spinner centered inside a confirmation modal that is processing. The modal stays open; the action button changes to a spinner; the content area shows a centered spinner with "Processing your investment..." Spinner: Ring L. Combine with copy that explains what is being processed.

### Pattern 4 - Page-level branded loading (XL SafqahBrand)

Used on app boot, after authentication, during onboarding transitions, and during deal-purchase confirmation flows. The SafqahBrand spinner ties the loading state to the brand identity. Centered on a full-screen overlay with a brief copy line ("Setting up your portfolio...") below. Use sparingly - overuse dilutes the branded feel.

### Pattern 5 - Chat / messaging typing indicator (M BouncingDots)

BouncingDots inside a chat-message bubble to indicate the AI agent or counterparty is composing a response. The dots sit inside an Alert-style bubble. Spinner: BouncingDots M. Subtle, casual, conversational.

### Motion - animation behavior

Spinners do not animate in Figma - they show their at-rest visual identity. The keyframe sequences below show how each spinner is intended to animate. The Code examples section below provides working CSS and Flutter implementations.

Motion Keyframe Sequences

Each spinner at Large (48px) across 4 keyframes. Real implementations interpolate smoothly between these frames; Figma can only show discrete snapshots. See the doc page for the underlying CSS / Flutter animation code.

> **Info:** Animation timing: Ring uses 0.8s linear infinite for smooth rotation. DotOrbit 1s linear. WaveBars per-bar 0.6s ease-in-out with 80ms phase stagger. BouncingDots per-dot 0.8s ease-in-out with 200ms phase stagger. PulseRings per-ring 1.4s ease-out with 333ms phase stagger. SquareMorph 1s linear. Hourglass 1.5s ease-in-out (heavier feel). SafqahBrand 1.6s ease-in-out for the coin-rise animation.

> **Warning:** Disable all spinner animations when the user has prefers-reduced-motion enabled. Show a static at-rest spinner. Replace with a textual "Loading..." message if possible.

> **Tip:** Show spinners only when work takes longer than 200ms. Below that threshold, the spinner flashes briefly and creates more anxiety than no indicator. Pair with a setTimeout: only render the spinner if the promise has not resolved by 200ms.

> **Tip:** These spinner components ARE prototypes. Each spinner set has two variant axes: Size (XS / S / M / L / XL) and Phase (0–3, the animation keyframe). Phase=0 is the default at-rest state. Each variant has a built-in Smart Animate reaction cycling Phase=0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 0, looping forever. Drop a spinner instance into a mockup (it starts at Phase=0) and press Play (▶) on any frame containing it - the spinner animates in place. Designers can ignore the Phase axis; it is internal animation machinery. Pick the Size variant you need, leave Phase=0 by default, and the animation just works.

### Code examples - CSS & Flutter

### Ring - CSS

```dart
.syntropy-spinner-ring {
  width: 32px;
  height: 32px;
  border: 2.5px solid transparent;
  border-top-color: var(--bg-brand-primary);
  border-right-color: var(--bg-brand-primary);
  border-bottom-color: var(--bg-brand-primary);
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: ring-spin 0.8s linear infinite;
}

@keyframes ring-spin {
  to { transform: rotate(360deg); }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .syntropy-spinner-ring { animation: none; }
}
```

### Ring - Flutter

```dart
class SyntropySpinnerRing extends StatelessWidget {
  final double size;
  const SyntropySpinnerRing({super.key, this.size = 32});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final strokeWidth = size <= 16 ? 1.5 : size <= 24 ? 2.0 : size <= 32 ? 2.5 : size <= 48 ? 3.5 : 4.5;
    return SizedBox(
      width: size,
      height: size,
      child: CircularProgressIndicator(
        strokeWidth: strokeWidth,
        valueColor: AlwaysStoppedAnimation(SyntropyTheme.of(context).brand.primary),
        // Flutter default already shows ~270° arc rotating
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### DotOrbit - CSS

```dart
.syntropy-spinner-dot-orbit {
  width: 32px;
  height: 32px;
  position: relative;
  animation: orbit-rotate 1s linear infinite;
}

.syntropy-spinner-dot-orbit .dot {
  position: absolute;

.syntropy-spinner-dot-orbit .dot:nth-child(2) { transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(30deg) translate(0, -11.2px); opacity: 0.7; }
.syntropy-spinner-dot-orbit .dot:nth-child(3) { transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(150deg) translate(0, -11.2px); opacity: 0.4; }

@keyframes orbit-rotate {
  to { transform: rotate(360deg); }
}
```

### DotOrbit - Flutter

```dart
class SyntropySpinnerDotOrbit extends StatefulWidget {
  final double size;
  const SyntropySpinnerDotOrbit({super.key, this.size = 32});

  @override
  State<SyntropySpinnerDotOrbit> createState() => _SyntropySpinnerDotOrbitState();
}

class _SyntropySpinnerDotOrbitState extends State<SyntropySpinnerDotOrbit> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late final AnimationController _controller;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _controller = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: const Duration(seconds: 1))..repeat();
  }

  @override
  void dispose() { _controller.dispose(); super.dispose(); }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final color = SyntropyTheme.of(context).brand.primary;
    return RotationTransition(
      turns: _controller,
      child: SizedBox(
        width: widget.size, height: widget.size,
        child: Stack(children: [
          for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
            Align(
              alignment: Alignment(
                math.cos((-math.pi / 2) + (i * math.pi * 2 / 3)),
                math.sin((-math.pi / 2) + (i * math.pi * 2 / 3)),
              ),
              child: Container(
                width: widget.size * 0.20, height: widget.size * 0.20,
                decoration: BoxDecoration(
                  color: color.withOpacity(1 - i * 0.3),
                  shape: BoxShape.circle,
                ),
              ),
            ),
        ]),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### WaveBars - Flutter

```dart
class SyntropySpinnerWaveBars extends StatefulWidget {
  final double size;
  const SyntropySpinnerWaveBars({super.key, this.size = 32});

  @override
  State<SyntropySpinnerWaveBars> createState() => _State();
}

class _State extends State<SyntropySpinnerWaveBars> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late final AnimationController _c;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _c = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 600))..repeat(reverse: true);
  }

  @override
  void dispose() { _c.dispose(); super.dispose(); }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final color = SyntropyTheme.of(context).brand.primary;
    final barW = widget.size * 0.08;
    return SizedBox(
      width: widget.size, height: widget.size * 0.7,
      child: Row(
        mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.spaceEvenly,
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.center,
        children: List.generate(5, (i) => AnimatedBuilder(
          animation: _c,
          builder: (_, __) {
            final phase = (_c.value + i * 0.08) % 1.0;
            final scale = 0.4 + 0.6 * (math.sin(phase * math.pi));
            return Container(
              width: barW,
              height: widget.size * 0.7 * scale,
              decoration: BoxDecoration(color: color, borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(barW / 2)),
            );
          },
        )),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### BouncingDots - Flutter

```dart
class SyntropySpinnerBouncingDots extends StatefulWidget {
  final double size;
  const SyntropySpinnerBouncingDots({super.key, this.size = 32});

  @override
  State<SyntropySpinnerBouncingDots> createState() => _BouncingState();
}

class _BouncingState extends State<SyntropySpinnerBouncingDots> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late final AnimationController _c;
  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _c = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 800))..repeat();
  }
  @override
  void dispose() { _c.dispose(); super.dispose(); }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final color = SyntropyTheme.of(context).brand.primary;
    final dotR = widget.size * 0.12;
    return SizedBox(
      width: widget.size, height: widget.size,
      child: AnimatedBuilder(
        animation: _c,
        builder: (_, __) => Row(
          mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.center,
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.center,
          children: List.generate(3, (i) {
            final phase = (_c.value - i * 0.25) % 1.0;
            final dy = -widget.size * 0.15 * math.max(0, math.sin(phase * math.pi));
            return Padding(
              padding: EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: dotR * 0.3),
              child: Transform.translate(
                offset: Offset(0, dy),
                child: Container(width: dotR * 2, height: dotR * 2, decoration: BoxDecoration(color: color, shape: BoxShape.circle)),
              ),
            );
          }),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

class SyntropySpinnerPulseRings extends StatefulWidget {
  final double size;
  const SyntropySpinnerPulseRings({super.key, this.size = 32});

  @override
  State<SyntropySpinnerPulseRings> createState() => _PulseState();
}

class _PulseState extends State<SyntropySpinnerPulseRings> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late final AnimationController _c;
  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _c = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 1400))..repeat();
  }
  @override
  void dispose() { _c.dispose(); super.dispose(); }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final color = SyntropyTheme.of(context).brand.primary;
    return SizedBox(
      width: widget.size, height: widget.size,
      child: AnimatedBuilder(
        animation: _c,
        builder: (_, __) => Stack(children: List.generate(3, (i) {
          final phase = (_c.value + i * 0.33) % 1.0;
          final scale = 0.3 + 0.7 * phase;
          final opacity = 1.0 - phase;
          return Center(
            child: Transform.scale(
              scale: scale,
              child: Container(
                width: widget.size, height: widget.size,
                decoration: BoxDecoration(
                  shape: BoxShape.circle,
                  border: Border.all(color: color.withOpacity(opacity), width: 1.5),
                ),
              ),
            ),
          );
        })),
      ),
    );
  }
}

### Hourglass - Flutter

```dart
class SyntropySpinnerHourglass extends StatefulWidget {
  final double size;
  const SyntropySpinnerHourglass({super.key, this.size = 32});

  @override
  State<SyntropySpinnerHourglass> createState() => _HourglassState();
}

class _HourglassState extends State<SyntropySpinnerHourglass> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late final AnimationController _c;
  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _c = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 1500))..repeat();
  }
  @override
  void dispose() { _c.dispose(); super.dispose(); }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final color = SyntropyTheme.of(context).brand.primary;
    return SizedBox(
      width: widget.size, height: widget.size,
      child: AnimatedBuilder(
        animation: _c,
        builder: (_, __) {
          final t = Curves.easeInOut.transform(_c.value);
          return Transform.rotate(
            angle: t * math.pi,
            child: CustomPaint(
              size: Size(widget.size, widget.size),
              painter: _HourglassPainter(color: color),
            ),
          );
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}

class _HourglassPainter extends CustomPainter {
  final Color color;
  _HourglassPainter({required this.color});
  @override
  void paint(Canvas canvas, Size size) {
    final paint = Paint()..color = color..style = PaintingStyle.fill;
    final pad = size.width * 0.15;
    final mid = size.width / 2;
    // Top triangle
    canvas.drawPath(Path()..moveTo(pad, pad)..lineTo(size.width - pad, pad)..lineTo(mid, mid)..close(), paint);
    // Bottom triangle
    canvas.drawPath(Path()..moveTo(mid, mid)..lineTo(size.width - pad, size.height - pad)..lineTo(pad, size.height - pad)..close(), paint);
  }
  @override
  bool shouldRepaint(_) => false;
}
```

### SafqahBrand - Flutter

```dart
class SyntropySpinnerSafqahBrand extends StatefulWidget {
  final double size;
  const SyntropySpinnerSafqahBrand({super.key, this.size = 32});

  @override
  State<SyntropySpinnerSafqahBrand> createState() => _BrandState();
}

class _BrandState extends State<SyntropySpinnerSafqahBrand> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late final AnimationController _c;
  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _c = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 1600))..repeat();
  }
  @override
  void dispose() { _c.dispose(); super.dispose(); }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final color = SyntropyTheme.of(context).brand.primary;
    final coinW = widget.size * 0.6;
    final coinH = widget.size * 0.18;
    final coins = [
      {'top': 0.65, 'opacity': 0.4, 'phase': 0.0},
      {'top': 0.45, 'opacity': 0.7, 'phase': 0.125},
      {'top': 0.20, 'opacity': 1.0, 'phase': 0.25},
    ];
    return SizedBox(
      width: widget.size, height: widget.size,
      child: AnimatedBuilder(
        animation: _c,
        builder: (_, __) => Stack(children: coins.map((c) {
          final phase = (_c.value + (c['phase'] as double)) % 1.0;
          final dy = -widget.size * 0.05 * math.sin(phase * math.pi * 2);
          return Positioned(
            top: widget.size * (c['top'] as double) + dy,
            left: (widget.size - coinW) / 2,
            child: Container(
              width: coinW, height: coinH,
              decoration: BoxDecoration(
                color: color.withOpacity(c['opacity'] as double),
                borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.elliptical(coinW / 2, coinH / 2)),
              ),
            ),
          );
        }).toList()),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Loader is NEW in Syntropy v2.0. The legacy Global_Design_System had no dedicated spinner component - loaders were ad-hoc CSS or Flutter CircularProgressIndicator instances with inconsistent styling. The 8 Syntropy spinners replace that ad-hoc usage with a canonical set.

> **Warning:** Spinners do NOT animate in Figma. They show their at-rest visual identity only. The animation is implemented in code (CSS keyframes, Flutter AnimationController). The Motion section embeds keyframe sequence frames showing 4 frozen frames of each animation cycle to communicate the intended motion to engineering.

> **Tip:** Use Ring 95% of the time. It is the canonical Syntropy spinner. The other 7 spinners exist for specific contexts: SafqahBrand for branded loading surfaces (app boot, onboarding, deal-purchase confirmations); SquareMorph or Hourglass for distinctive non-circular contexts; DotOrbit or BouncingDots for chat / messaging / typing indicators; WaveBars for audio / media contexts; PulseRings for radar / scanning / detection contexts. Mixing spinner styles in the same product feels chaotic. Pick one per surface and use it consistently.

> **Info:** For button-internal loading states (the most common loader use case), use the Button component's built-in State=loading variant instead of placing a separate Loader inside a Button. The Button already wires up the spinner correctly and handles label-to-spinner swap during loading.

> **Warning:** Show spinners only when work takes longer than 200ms. Below that threshold, the spinner flashes briefly which creates more anxiety than no indicator at all. Pair the spinner mount with a 200ms setTimeout - only render if the promise has not resolved by then.

> **Tip:** Skeletons preserve layout shape and are better than spinners for list / grid / card loading. Use Skeleton (05e) for those contexts. Use spinners only when the shape of the result is irrelevant or unpredictable (modal processing, button submitting, page-level transition).

> **Warning:** For loads longer than 10 seconds, do NOT use an indeterminate spinner. Show concrete progress (percentage, step count, ETA) using ProgressBar (04j) or a steps indicator. A spinner running for 30 seconds reads as "broken" to users.

> **Tip:** The SafqahBrand spinner is the only one that uses brand semantics directly (stacked coin discs tying to the Safqah investment theme). Use sparingly - overuse dilutes the branded feel. Reserve for moments where product personality should come through (app boot, post-investment confirmation, onboarding).

> **Warning:** Always disable spinner animation when prefers-reduced-motion is enabled. Show a static at-rest spinner instead. Better still, show a textual "Loading..." or "Saving..." indicator that does not animate at all.
